answer:
The `POST /articles` endpoint is handled by the `create_new_article` function in `app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py` [E3, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:53].

When this endpoint is called:
1.  It expects a request body containing article data, which is validated against `ArticleInCreate` and is expected to be embedded under the alias `"article"` [E3, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:60].
2.  It requires the current authenticated user, obtained via `get_current_user_authorizer()` [E3, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:61].
3.  It depends on an instance of `ArticlesRepository`, which is provided by `get_repository(ArticlesRepository)` [E3, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:62].
4.  It first calls `get_slug_for_article(article_create.title)` to generate a slug from the provided title [E3, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:64].
5.  It checks if an article with that slug already exists by calling `check_article_exists(articles_repo, slug)` [E3, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65]. If it exists, it raises an `HTTPException` with status 400 [E3, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:66-69].
6.  If the slug is unique, it calls `articles_repo.create_article(...)` to persist the new article [E3, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:71]. This call passes the generated `slug`, the `title`, `description`, `body`, the `author` (the current user), and the `tags` [E3, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:72-77].
7.  Finally, it returns the newly created article wrapped in `ArticleInResponse`, using `ArticleForResponse.from_orm(article)` to format the response [E3, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:79].
